function: Reads the markdown string produced by _markdown() and the PDF that follows it, not workers/lab.json. Asserts, per section: that no section body parses as a JSON object or array; that no line matches the serialized-object signature (a lone '{', '[', or a '"key": value' line at indent); that every section declared by the unit prose contract is present as prose; and that no build-time placeholder string (for example 'Draft pending downstream human review.') survives into a shipped artifact. Emits a per-section PASS/FAIL list and blocks emission of the PDF on any FAIL, so the defect cannot reach a page render.
what_makes_it_sota: arXiv 2605.02363 ('When Correct Isn't Usable') names the structured-output reliability gap and measures it as up to 85% task accuracy on GSM8K against 0% output accuracy, establishing that correctness of content and usability of the delivered artifact are separate properties requiring separate measurement. arXiv 2604.09691 (CAGE) shows the same discipline in educational media: because free generation 'catastrophically garbles text labels', correctness is anchored to the deterministic step and verified on its output rather than assumed.
role_in_curriculum_builder: Runs inside runtime/session_bridge.py finalize(), after unit_checks.json is written (currently line 258) and immediately before the 'Render selected unit draft to shipped PDF' step (currently line 262). It takes the output of _markdown() (runtime/session_bridge.py:201) as its input and gates the render, making it the first check in the pipeline whose input is the consumed artifact rather than an intermediate object.
issues_resolved: QA report, Critical: 'Document renderer dumps raw JSON as lesson body. All 4 lessons (L01-L04). Sections under "Engage/Explore/Explain/..." contain literal structured objects instead of prose', quoting L01/document/L01.md:15-19. Root cause is runtime/session_bridge.py:211, json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) into the markdown body, with lines 212-214 doing the same for identification, troubleshooting and safety. All four of L01's unit_checks.json entries passed regardless, because they read workers/lab.json. Also catches the placeholder line '*Draft pending downstream human review.*' hard-coded at runtime/session_bridge.py:203 into every shipped document.

function: Tokenises the rendered lesson text (not the lab.json declaration), computes Flesch-Kincaid grade level and sentence/word-length distributions against the curriculum's declared target band, and diffs the document's content words against the union of this unit's declared vocabulary and all terms defined in prior units. Emits the measured grade level, the list of undefined terms in excess of the per-lab cap with their line numbers, and a PASS/FAIL. Blocks acceptance of the unit on either a band miss or a cap breach.
what_makes_it_sota: arXiv 2309.05454 ('Flesch or Fumble?') evaluates instruction-tuned models against FKGL and CEFR under standard-guided prompts and finds that 'globally recognized models like ChatGPT may be considered less effective and may require more refined prompts', establishing that a stated target band is not a delivered band. arXiv 2501.09158 shows the failure concentrates at exactly the bands this curriculum targets: 'variable utility in grade level accuracy and consistency of keywords and key phrases when attempting to level content down to the fourth grade reading level.'
role_in_curriculum_builder: This is the unimplemented TEXT-READABILITY-BAND check that prompt.md already declares mandatory for every unit in every subject. It runs as a gate-2 deterministic check per unit, writing its verdict into results/unit_checks.json alongside LAB-SCHEMA-VALID, and it must run after the Rendered Document Conformance Reviewer, since measuring readability on a JSON dump is meaningless.
issues_resolved: QA report, Critical: 'results/unit_checks.json for every lesson (L01-L04) contains only DOMAIN-SCHEMA-VALID, DOMAIN-VERIFIER, LAB-SCHEMA-VALID, RECEIPT-HASH-RESOLVES. No TEXT-READABILITY-BAND ... Nothing in the pipeline could have caught the level mismatch even if the text had rendered as prose.' And QA, High: 'L04 (document/L04.md:26-27,59,89): mAVΩ, 10A socket, mode dial, fuse — 4+ undefined terms against a cap of 2', against a stated target of 'age 9+, Flesch-Kincaid grade 2-6, ≤2 new terms/lab' and a reported symptom that output 'reads at level 100'.

function: Independently classifies each learning objective's cognitive level from its statement, its success criterion and the Explore/Evaluate tasks that actually operationalise it, then compares that classification against the self-reported pedagogy.learning_objectives[].bloom_level. Emits a per-objective agreement/disagreement verdict, and a run-level distribution showing whether cognitive demand varies across the unit sequence. Fails a unit when a declared level is contradicted by its own task verbs; warns at run level when the level distribution is constant across units of differing type.
what_makes_it_sota: arXiv 2306.17459 analysed 127 GPT-4-authored learning objectives and found well-formed ones 'largely operate at the appropriate level of Bloom's taxonomy, respecting the different nature of the conceptual modules (lower levels) and projects (higher levels)' — differentiation by unit type is the published signature of reasoned objectives. arXiv 2606.13684 (AIED 2026) establishes the right classifier architecture for a multi-subject pipeline: 'Supervised ML/DL models degraded substantially on unseen datasets' whereas prompted LLMs 'were more stable', best with in-context examples plus course-specific action verbs.
role_in_curriculum_builder: This is the unimplemented TEXT-BLOOM-VERBS check that prompt.md declares mandatory. It runs as a gate-2 per-unit check writing into results/unit_checks.json, reading workers/lab.json's pedagogy block plus the rendered document, and it additionally contributes a run-level distribution to the run root beside results/gate_1_static_preflight.json.
issues_resolved: QA report, Critical: unit_checks.json for every lesson has 'no TEXT-BLOOM-VERBS, despite prompt.md naming both as mandatory gate-2 checks run "on every unit in every subject."' Beyond the QA report, this scan found that all four units declare the identical bloom_level triple [remember, understand, apply] in workers/lab.json, and that L01's third objective is declared 'apply' while the tasks backing it are 'Point to the source lead end', 'Point to the module DC input' and 'Trace the three dashed teaching links ... with a finger' — recognition, not application. The bloom_level field is populated and schema-valid and read by no check.

function: For each entry in the unit's visuals array, checks the image against the caption and the unit's identification.technical_name that it claims to depict, and additionally checks the asset digest against digests used by other units in the same run to detect an asset reused across units with incompatible subjects. Emits, per visual, an alignment verdict plus the specific mismatch when it fails; blocks the unit when a visual whose role is subject_identification does not depict the unit's declared subject.
what_makes_it_sota: Gordon et al., 'Mismatch Quest' (ECCV 2024, arXiv 2312.03766), establishes that 'existing image-text alignment models reach high quality binary assessments' while falling short of 'pinpointing the exact source of misalignment' — meaning binary alignment scoring is mature enough to deploy today, with localisation as an upgrade rather than a prerequisite. arXiv 2604.09691 (CAGE) supplies the risk model: label and content fidelity in educational imagery is a distinct property from the image existing, protected by anchoring to deterministic structure.
role_in_curriculum_builder: Runs in runtime/session_bridge.py finalize() immediately after check_receipts (currently line 256, implemented at runtime/checks.py:46) and before unit_checks.json is written, extending that step from hash resolution to depicted-content verification. Its cross-unit digest comparison needs the run root, so it reads sibling unit directories under the run output rather than the unit directory alone.
issues_resolved: Not in the QA report; found in this scan by hashing the assets. assets/official_reference.jpg is byte-identical across all four units — sha256 8f9ab6c86f259c4d8cc75066df4bba73ef895973bfd5e182316c2659cd964efc appears in the L01, L02, L03 and L04 manifest.json files — while serving as the '### Subject Identification' visual for four different subjects: a breadboard power-supply module, a solderless breadboard, male-to-male jumper wires and a digital multimeter. RECEIPT-HASH-RESOLVES reports PASS on all four, because it verifies that the digest resolves to a present file and never asks what the file depicts. The lessons depend on it directly, e.g. L04 step 3: 'Find the COM socket and note it always takes the black probe.'

function: Takes the whole set of completed units rather than one unit. Builds a forward-link graph from each unit's next_lab_link and a backward graph from pedagogy.prior_knowledge.prerequisite_labs, then asserts that the two agree, that every unit is reachable, that no unit is skipped by its predecessor's hand-off, that no successor is claimed by two units with incompatible promises, and that every referenced unit id exists in the curriculum manifest. Emits the broken edges and blocks the run from being marked complete.
what_makes_it_sota: Kristen Huff (Curriculum Associates), writing for the Center for Assessment, argues coherence must be built deliberately — 'Coherence is crucial to student learning. We must not leave it to chance', 'We rarely define coherence clearly, or design for it intentionally', and 'partial coherence is not coherence.' Kobrin et al. (2015) make structure one of four explicit criteria a learning progression must be evaluated against. arXiv 2605.09635 (K12-KGraph) shows current practice modelling curriculum structure as explicit relations — nine node types and fourteen relation types, with a dedicated 'Prereq' benchmark task family — rather than leaving prerequisite claims in unit prose.
role_in_curriculum_builder: A new run-level gate, executed after all units finish and writing to the run root beside results/gate_1_static_preflight.json. It is the pipeline's first check whose input is the set of units: every existing check in results/unit_checks.json is scoped to one unit, and runtime/session_bridge.py finalize() takes a single output directory, so no current gate can observe a link that points outside its own unit.
issues_resolved: Not in the QA report; found in this scan by reading the four next_lab_link values in order. L03 hands off to L05 — 'L05 asks you to plan a resistor's two connection points the same way this lab planned a wire's' — skipping L04 entirely, while L04 also claims L05: 'L05 uses the same evidence-first habit to read a resistor's value before any circuit is built.' L04 is therefore orphaned with nothing pointing into it, and L05 is double-claimed. results/gate_1_static_preflight.json confirms both L04 and L05 are real units in the 35-unit manifest, so this is a broken chain rather than a naming artefact.

function: The pipeline's subjective reviewer, instantiated on a model from a different family than the one that authored the unit. Reads the rendered lesson as a teacher would and returns a reasoned verdict on whether the lesson teaches what it claims, whether its explanation is honest at the target level, and whether its hinge question actually discriminates understanding. Also reviews units as a set, to surface exemplar-mirroring that per-unit scoring cannot see. Records the judging model's family alongside the verdict, and hard-fails the run rather than passing when no out-of-family judge is available.
what_makes_it_sota: arXiv 2508.06709 ('Play Favorites') controls for true quality with independent human evaluation and finds GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet 'systematically assign higher scores to their own outputs' and additionally 'display family-bias; systematically assigning higher ratings to outputs produced by other models of the same family' — the empirical basis for the cross-family requirement. arXiv 2410.21819 explains why the failure is silent rather than loud: judges prefer low-perplexity, familiar text, so a same-family judge returns a plausible PASS. arXiv 2306.10509 (Denny et al.) motivates set-level review, finding AI resources 'closely mirror the given exemplars' where human ones show 'greater variety'. arXiv 2508.19611 shows even autonomous multi-agent instructional design terminating in review by someone other than the generator.
role_in_curriculum_builder: Occupies the existing REV-JUDGE-SINGLE-CROSS-FAMILY slot, currently recorded as deferred RT-5 in policy/checks.v1.yaml. It runs after the deterministic gate-2 checks pass, per unit and then once over the run, and its availability must be resolved at routing time in runtime/routing.py so that an unavailable judge is a blocking condition rather than a recorded divergence.
issues_resolved: QA report, Critical: 'The one subjective quality check was bypassed identically on all 4 units.' acceptance.json for L01-L04 records '"routing_divergence": "USER_AUTHORIZED_IN_SESSION_MODEL; cross-family judge bypassed"' and routing/authoring.json gives '"decision_rationale": "user authorized the current in-session LLM as the model worker; no separate API"'. QA concludes 'REV-JUDGE-SINGLE-CROSS-FAMILY — the only check that reads output like a human would — never ran ... the pipeline's sole subjective gate was inert for the entire run.' The gap this agent closes is not only the missing judgement but the fact that its absence was survivable: the run completed and shipped four lessons with the bypass recorded as a note.
